/SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Issued at 245 AM CDT Sat Sep 19 2026

Shower and Storm Chances Continue Sunday Into Monday:
As the cold front continues pushing through the area from
northwest to southeast through the day on Sunday, shower and
thunderstorm chances will continue. Moisture will be best
furthest to the west even as the front progresses, so the best
instability (>1500 J/kg CAPE) will also likely remain in the
western portions of our area for storms to tap into. The
questions regarding extent of ongoing showers/storms and
residual cloud cover Sunday morning does translate into some
questions surrounding location and timing of storms, greatest
extent of coverage, and just how intense storms could get.
Regardless, with temperatures still in the 90s ahead of the
front and dew points increasing by 10+ degrees with frontal
passage, re-initiation of storms is expected to some degree by
the afternoon as a reinforcing vort max from the upper trough
pushes across the region. Once storms re-initiate Sunday
afternoon, rainfall will likely continue overnight into Monday 
as the front slowly slides further southeast out of the area.

Vertical wind profiles are generally unimpressive, with upper-
level impulses generally restricted to shortwave intrusions
along the northern periphery of the ridge that flattens into Ark-
La-Tex through the weekend rather than the support of an
organized jet streak. However, remnant enhancements from
nocturnal low-level jet streak activity may locally enhance 
shear to 30-40kts as the jet streaks are advected into our 
area, increasing shear enough that organized cold pools could 
briefly develop and support severe winds to 60 mph. If shear >40
kts can overlap with areas where MUCAPE >2000 J/kg AND storms
form within that overlap, elevated storms would have the
potential to produce hail up to quarter to ping pong sized, but
this risk appears more conditional at this time. The most likely
time period for this overlap would be Sunday afternoon into
early evening.

Convection still appears to not be continuous in time or space
throughout the day Sunday, with all-day washouts still appearing
unlikely; it appears more likely that multiple rounds of 
strengthening and diminishing showers and storms will occur
throughout Sunday and even into Monday. Most areas are expected
to see between 0.25-0.75", with low end (10th percentile)
amounts of 0-0.1" and high end amounts (90th percentile) of
1.25-2" in most areas (per NBM). Highly localized bullseyes of 
2+ inches seem plausible in areas that see strong storms or 
repeated rounds of rainfall, with 00Z HREF LPMMs further
indicating very localized pockets of 2+ inches could occur
somewhere. Even so, considering recent drought, soils will be
capable of soaking up 2" easily, so flash flooding is not
expected with these storms. Highest rainfall totals are still
anticipated to align with areas of highest overall moisture
north of I-44.

Heat Sunday, But Then It's Done:
As the cold front moves through on Sunday, it will finally start
cooling things off. However, far southern and eastern portions
of our area may not see the front until Sunday night, so
depending cloud cover, moisture return, and frontal progression 
by Sunday morning, temperatures on Sunday may remain in the 90s 
for a final day in some areas. Due to this uncertainty, opted 
not to extend the Heat Advisory into Sunday at this time, but it
still remains a possibility, depending on how the situation 
evolves over the next 24 hours.

However, Monday finally brings temperatures back down below 90
degrees, with a temperature gradient ranging from upper 70s in
west-central and central Missouri to mid- to upper 80s in
south-central Missouri as the frontal influence lingers across
the eastern Ozarks. Tuesday has seasonally appropriate
temperatures in the mid- to upper 70s areawide, with lows in the
50s. These temperatures look to continue through the work week,
with PoPs remaining below 20% through Thursday.
